detail.longDescription: A few weeks ago, we announced [1] our work, "File Notification Attacks" [ https:// inoti.fyi/ ], which will be presented at CCS'26 (Technical Session C4) between 16.00-18.00 next Monday, Nov/16, 2026. CCS'26 will be held in The Hague, Netherlands... and yes, my advisor ( @ lavados ) was going to send me there anyway for the occasional crimes against science I've committed and the general bad science that I perform... (/j). Since our announcement a few weeks ago, we've found that our research extends to FreeBSD too -- now pre-mitigated [2] --, (thanks to @ lattera for suggesting that!), and illumos as well -- also mitigated [3] -- (thanks @ wiedi for that). It's quite interesting that multiple kernels and independent implementations over the past decades have had similar-but-vastly-different issues 🧐🤔. Our artifacts have also been evaluated by reviewers to be Available, Evaluated (Functional), and Reproduced. Check them out at Zenodo: https:// zenodo.org/records/22843469 or give it a 🌟 on GitHub: https:// github.com/isec-tugraz/file-no tification-attacks It's pretty cool that we got such wide-spread coverage about our research (there's a new media section on our website)! If you're at CCS'26 and work on any systems security, feel free to hmu and it'd be cool to meet there :D I'll be announcing a new (Linux defense) paper that's been accepted at NDSS'27 (Seoul, South Korea!!!) soon-ish :D Thanks to my co-authors Xufan Zhao, Jeanette Wultsch, @ hweissi , Florian Draschbacher, @ notbobbytables , and @ lavados !!!
